info.name: madlad
info.description:
MADLAD-400 translation service (madlad-api), called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/madlad` → `http://madlad-api:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET+POST, headers forwarded). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth.

Direct access: if you don't want to go through LiteLLM, override the URL of individual requests to `{{madlad}}` — that variable points at madlad-api's host-published port (default localhost:8008 via PORT_MADLAD_API). The direct path is unauthenticated by default; the /v1/madlad LiteLLM path is authenticated by the virtual key. See ai/madlad/MADLAD.md for the operator guide and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Endpoints: GET /languages (list ~400 supported target codes), POST /translate (auto-detect source, translate to target), GET /health (liveness), plus MCP JSON-RPC at /mcp/ exposing the `translate` tool. Note the request body uses `target_lang` — source language is auto-detected, there is no `src` field.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host. Prefix all pass-through requests with {{litellm}}/v1/madlad/… — LiteLLM strips /v1/madlad and forwards the rest to madlad-api on ai_shared.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the /v1/madlad pass-through — most keys created for chat models already do. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

Direct-access base URL for madlad-api (bypasses LiteLLM). Host-published port is PORT_MADLAD_API (default 8008); on ai_shared it's http://madlad-api:8000. No auth is enforced at this layer — use only for local debugging inside a trusted network. Swap `{{litellm}}/v1/madlad` for `{{madlad}}` in any request URL to talk to the service directly.
MCP transport session id — paste in the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie.

request.description: Liveness probe on madlad-api (the proxy container). Returns {"status": "ok"} once the FastAPI app has started — does NOT verify madlad-app (the inference container) is reachable, since the model is lazy-loaded on the first /translate or /languages call. Docker's own healthcheck for madlad-api polls this endpoint. See MADLAD.md § Health check.

List the ~400 target languages MADLAD-400 supports. Response shape: {"languages": [{"code": "af", "name": "Afrikaans"}, {"code": "am", "name": "Amharic"}, …]}. Codes are ISO 639-1 where available, ISO 639-3 for low-resource languages, occasionally with a regional suffix (e.g. `zh_CN`). Names are resolved via the `langcodes` library. Use a returned `code` as `target_lang` in POST /translate.

First call after container start triggers the lazy model download (~1-3 min for the ~3 GB CT2 checkpoint). Subsequent calls are instant. Proxied to madlad-app's /languages inside the ai_shared network; returns 502 with `Cannot reach madlad-app: …` if the inference container is down. See MADLAD.md § Supported languages.

Translate a single string. Body: {"text": string, "target_lang": string}. Source language is auto-detected by MADLAD — there is no `src` field. `target_lang` must be one of the codes returned by GET /languages (ISO 639-1 preferred, e.g. `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `zh`, `de`, `pt`, `ar`, `hi`, `ko`).

Response shape: {"translated": "<string>"}. First call after container start triggers the ~1-3 min lazy load. Steady-state latency is dominated by the model forward pass; the beam-search + repetition guards default to ~3-4× a greedy decode (see MADLAD.md § Decoding parameters for the current beam_size=4 / repetition_penalty=1.1 / no_repeat_ngram_size=3 / max_decoding_length=1024 defaults and when to tune).

Errors: 400 for malformed JSON, 422 for missing fields, 502 with `Cannot reach madlad-app: …` if the inference container is unreachable. See MADLAD.md § Usage.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises madlad-api as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.madlad_translate` in litellm_config.yaml (transport: http, url: http://madlad-api:8000/mcp) — models see the `translate` tool through that path, not this one. The Postman requests below are for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

Unlike a chat completions model, MADLAD is tool-only — it does not appear in `model_list` and cannot be called via /v1/chat/completions directly. Use it by asking a chat model to invoke the `translate` tool, then loop the tool result back (see CLAUDE.md § LiteLLM with Phoenix MCP for the two-step pattern).

request.description: MCP handshake. Response headers include `mcp-session-id` — copy it into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable. Response body is a JSON-RPC result advertising FastMCP's server info + capabilities.

Enumerate available tools. madlad-api exposes exactly one: `translate(text: str, target_lang: str) -> str`. `text` is the source (any language, auto-detected); `target_lang` is an ISO 639-1 code (see GET /languages). Returns the translated string, or an `Error translating: …` string on upstream failure (the MCP tool does not raise — it swallows the httpx error into the return value).

Invoke the `translate` tool via MCP. Result body has a text-content block containing the translated string (e.g. `おはよう` for the example). Equivalent in effect to POST /translate — same lazy-load behavior on the first call, same beam-search decoding defaults. Difference is transport: this path is what chat models routed through LiteLLM's mcp_servers.madlad_translate hit when they decide to translate mid-conversation. See MADLAD.md § LiteLLM integration for the chat-completions → tool-call round-trip pattern.
